# A good demo, but we need support that works
**★☆☆☆☆ — One star for now**

Bridger Bend Community Library is a one-branch library with two full-time staff, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June 2026 at $14,200 per year. Our catalog and circulation migration went live October 19.

Since October 28, checkouts have worked only in offline mode on one laptop. Our holds queue was wiped, with approximately 640 holds lost. Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We have received three replies, each saying the issue has been “escalated to engineering.” We still need a working system and someone who will take responsibility for getting us there.

During sales, we were promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” What we received was a shared inbox.

These failures have consequences beyond staff inconvenience. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to collect his held large-print Westerns. We had no record of his hold and sent him home with nothing. A volunteer has been recording checkouts on index cards. With two full-time staff, we cannot absorb this much extra work without taking time away from patrons.

To be fair, the software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is better than our old system. My concern is not the product idea. It is the support we have received when essential services stopped working.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and our library’s line item is on the agenda. I need to be able to explain what is being done to restore the service we are paying for.

I am asking a senior person at Stackhouse to call me this week, name a person responsible for our case, and provide a written recovery plan addressing circulation and the missing holds, with timelines and regular updates.

For other small-library directors: get support response times, escalation procedures, and migration staffing commitments in writing before signing. Ask what happens when circulation fails—not just how it works in a demo.

One star reflects our experience so far. I will revisit this review if Stackhouse resolves these problems and follows through on support.
